text.arabic_uthmani: صِرَٰطَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ ٱلْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا ٱلضَّآلِّينَ

words.gloss_range: the same requested path from 1:6, now locally specified as the route of a favored community and bounded by exclusions rather than introduced as a new sentence
words.root_gloss_range: a path or broad route field with pressure from passage, roadway, and engulfing imagery; the local ayah selects the moral-guidance route, not an isolated concrete bridge sense
words.prose: {{ar:صِرَٰطَ}} ({{tr:ṣirāṭa}}) opens without a new verb, so the ayah stays inside the guidance request of 1:6 and identifies the requested object by apposition. The path is not an abstract line only: the {{ar:ص ر ط}} ({{tr:ṣ-r-ṭ}}) pressure lets the route feel like a channel one enters and is carried through, while local usage keeps it in the moral-guidance path range rather than a concrete bridge. Its first position turns the earlier straight path into a populated route, first marked by favor and then bounded by two exclusions; its heavy onset also makes the word feel like an audible threshold rather than isolated vocabulary.

topics.headline: cross-ayah appositive path specification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees 1:7 as a specification of the already requested path in 1:6, not as a separate new petition.
topics.reason: The accusative noun and appositional chain are licensed by the prior guidance request and immediately define the same path through its people and limits.

topics.headline: roadway and engulfing pressure within the path sense
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the path as a route that channels and carries travelers, while still reading the local noun as the moral-guidance path.
topics.reason: Root and distribution evidence support roadway and engulfing pressure, but the local profile keeps this occurrence in the dominant abstract path use rather than a concrete bridge reading.

topics.headline: path cooccurs with guidance and favor fields
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this path is defined by bestowed favor, not only by formal straightness.
topics.reason: The critical rows link the path field with guidance and favor, and the local construct immediately defines the path by those upon whom favor was bestowed.

topics.headline: heavy onset marks the path threshold
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the opening path word as a weighty threshold into the ayah's specification.
topics.reason: The onset variants do not change the referent, but they make the first consonant a noticeable recitational pressure point.

topics.headline: hapax signal limited to surface slot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader avoids treating the path word as lexically isolated and instead focuses on its unusual slot at the start of the ayah.
topics.reason: The occurrence evidence blocks a global rarity claim for the lexeme or root, so the useful rarity is only the bare accusative path word reopening the prior object.

words.gloss_range: definite masculine plural relative pronoun in a genitive construct chain, identifying the path through a group defined by the favor clause that follows
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) makes the path belong to a described community rather than to a bare label. The relative pronoun opens the clause of received favor, so the positive class is recognized through what happened to them. Its plural definiteness keeps the reference collective, while a recited onset contraction can tighten the sound boundary without changing that collective grammar. The boundary from the speakers' request to the favored them makes the prayer relational.

topics.headline: relative pronoun defines the path's people by a clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the favored group is not named by title but defined through a following event of favor.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the relative pronoun the genitive complement of the path noun and the opener of the relative clause.

topics.headline: received plural keeps a recognizable collective
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the received wording as a definite collective rather than a singular-generic open reference.
topics.reason: The variant contrast clarifies that the local form preserves masculine plural collective reference.

topics.headline: elided-onset variant tightens the construct link
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears how recitation can tighten the boundary between the path noun and the relative pronoun without changing the grammar.
topics.reason: The variant affects the audible boundary while preserving the construct relation.

topics.headline: petitioning us is oriented toward favored them
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the prayer's pronoun movement from the speakers' us toward a distinct favored them.
topics.reason: The relative group begins the positive them toward whom the prior request seeks alignment.

words.gloss_range: completed second-person divine bestowal of favor onto the group, with the favor-object compressed and the recipient expressed through the following upon-them phrase
words.root_gloss_range: a favor, ease, blessing, well-being, material good, and affirmation field; the local Form IV verb selects causative bestowal rather than mere comfort or verbal assent
words.prose: {{ar:أَنْعَمْتَ}} ({{tr:anʿamta}}) keeps God directly addressed even after the petition turns into path specification. The Form IV verb presents favor as something caused to rest upon the group, while the missing direct object leaves the gift itself compressed inside the verb and its following endpoint. The {{ar:ن ع م}} ({{tr:n-ʿ-m}}) field gives that favor a texture of ease and bestowed well-being, and the wider favored-class formula (4:69) can illuminate the category without replacing this ayah's compact direct address.

topics.headline: perfect verb sustains direct divine address
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that specification of the path still speaks directly to God rather than shifting into detached description.
topics.reason: The verb is perfect second masculine singular, and the discourse continues the direct address established in the preceding petition.

topics.headline: favor-object omitted into the upon-them frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels favor as an event and state bestowed on the group, not as a named object listed in the sentence.
topics.reason: The local verb has no overt direct object; the recipient endpoint carries the relation and leaves the favor itself implicit.

topics.headline: causative form transfers ease and favor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses favor as bestowed ease and well-being, while local morphology keeps the selected value as causative favor rather than every root branch at once.
topics.reason: Root evidence supplies ease, blessing, wealth, and affirmation pressure, but the Form IV frame with the recipient phrase selects causative bestowal in this ayah.

topics.headline: recognized favored-class formula remains compact
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear a wider favored-class formula, including 4:69, while keeping this ayah's group structurally open.
topics.reason: The formulaic echo is real, but the local wording names the class by direct address and does not import the full 4:69 list as the only referent.

topics.headline: favor mediates the path and exclusions
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the path becoming a social-moral field populated by favored and excluded groups.
topics.reason: The cooccurrence and boundary rows converge with the local clause: the path is defined through favor before the exclusions are named.

words.gloss_range: upon-them prepositional complement marking the recipients as the locus of divine favor in the relative clause
words.prose: The first {{ar:عَلَيْهِمْ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhim}}) supplies the endpoint of favor: the group is grammatically the locus on which the bestowal rests. The preposition keeps its upon-direction audible, but in this verb frame it is benefactive. Suffix sound variants leave the favored them stable, so the speakers' request remains oriented toward that plurality. Because the same surface returns after the wrath participle, this first endpoint prepares an exact formal mirror whose charge will reverse.

topics.headline: upon-them marks recipient locus of favor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices favor landing on the group as a grammatical endpoint rather than a loose beneficiary added afterward.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the phrase the governed complement of the favor verb and locks the pronoun in the prepositional relation.

topics.headline: upon-direction becomes benefactive in the favor frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the same upon-direction that can later carry wrath, while local valence makes this occurrence benefactive.
topics.reason: The preposition retains directional pressure, but the governing verb selects the benefactive value here.

topics.headline: first endpoint prepares the opposite-valence mirror
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the exact repeated endpoint before recognizing that the semantic charge reverses in the second occurrence.
topics.reason: The ayah repeats the same preposition-pronoun surface after a positive and then a negative governing expression.

topics.headline: recipient suffix remains stable through recitational variants
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the requester's us oriented toward a stable favored them even where recitation varies the suffix sound.
topics.reason: The variants affect vowel length and color, not the 3mp reference; the pronoun contrast remains part of the request's relational movement.

words.gloss_range: genitive exceptive boundary marker embedded in the path chain, excluding the following negative classes while allowing the exclusion to qualify either the people or the path relation
words.root_gloss_range: otherness, exclusion, difference, change, and protective zeal fields; the local noun selects alterity and exception, with affective boundary pressure but not the verbal change sense
words.prose: {{ar:غَيْرِ}} ({{tr:ghayri}}) is the hinge where the ayah turns from the favored route to its boundaries. Its genitive case embeds exclusion inside the same nominal chain rather than making it a detached circumstance, while its attachment can be felt against either the favored group or the path relation. The {{ar:غ ي ر}} ({{tr:gh-y-r}}) field adds charged otherness, but the local noun selects exclusion and alterity, not verbal changing. Its initial sound also tightens the immediate move into the wrath class.

topics.headline: genitive case embeds exclusion with live attachment options
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that exclusion is built into the path chain, while the grammar leaves open whether it qualifies the people or the path relation.
topics.reason: The received genitive supports appositional or attributive attachment and blocks making the word a free accusative circumstance in the canonical parse.

topics.headline: alterity selected with affective boundary pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels exclusion as charged otherness, while the local form stays with the exceptive noun rather than the verbal change branch.
topics.reason: Dictionary and distribution evidence support alterity and affective zeal around the root, but local grammar selects the abstract exceptive noun.

topics.headline: single hinge pivots favor into double exclusion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah as a three-beat contrastive map rather than a positive phrase plus incidental cautions.
topics.reason: The word stands between the favor clause and the two excluded groups, and the following coordination extends its restrictive force.

topics.headline: initial sound carries exclusion into wrath naming
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a local sound tightening as exclusion moves immediately into the wrath category.
topics.reason: The row provides a local sound relation; it sharpens the transition but does not alter the syntactic parse.

words.gloss_range: definite passive participle naming the wrath-incurred class, with the affected recipients foregrounded and the wrath agent left unspoken
words.root_gloss_range: wrath, anger, swelling heat, and reactive force fields; the local passive participle selects those upon whom wrath is directed rather than narrating the act or naming the agent
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمَغْضُوبِ}} ({{tr:al-maghḍūbi}}) names a recognizable class by affected status: the passive participle foregrounds those bearing wrath while leaving the agent unspoken. The {{ar:غ ض ب}} ({{tr:gh-ḍ-b}}) field gives the class the feel of heated force directed onto a target. The formula recurs with the upon-construction in 2:61, 2:90, 3:112, and 5:60, while here it remains unnamed and open; it also mirrors the favor endpoint in this ayah by reversing benefaction into adversarial descent. As the first excluded class it stays distinct from final straying, and sound variants can harden its texture without changing the passive-recipient role.

topics.headline: definite passive participle foregrounds affected class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a known class defined by bearing wrath, not a freshly narrated anger event.
topics.reason: The local form is a definite passive participle in the genitive chain, and its agent is grammatically suppressed while the affected class is foregrounded.

topics.headline: heated rising root pressure colors wrath receipt
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels wrath as directed heated force while keeping the local sense in the passive wrath-recipient frame.
topics.reason: Root evidence supplies rising heat and swelling pressure, but the local participle selects the affected class rather than a physiological description.

topics.headline: recurrent formula appears without naming the group
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes the wrath-upon formula, including its recurrences in 2:61, 2:90, 3:112, and 5:60, while noticing that 1:7 leaves the group unnamed.
topics.reason: The formulaic parallels are concrete, and the 1:4 relation can frame final accountability, but neither supplies a named referent inside this ayah.

topics.headline: wrath class pairs with straying and mirrors favor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices two negative classes under one exclusion and hears the wrath phrase reverse the earlier favor endpoint.
topics.reason: The local construction repeats the same endpoint after the wrath participle, while the coordinated final class keeps wrath-reception distinct from straying.

topics.headline: emphatic-stop variant hardens sound without changing role
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the wrath word as an acoustic pressure point while the passive recipient role stays constant.
topics.reason: The sound variant changes texture but preserves the passive participial frame and referent role.

words.gloss_range: second upon-them complement, completing the passive wrath construction by marking the target on whom wrath is directed
words.prose: The second {{ar:عَلَيْهِمْ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhim}}) completes the wrath construction by giving the passive participle its target. The same upon-form now bears adversarial force, so the reader hears the earlier endpoint of favor return with its charge inverted. Local grammar favors the wrath-incurred group as the suffix referent; alternate fold-back readings remain contrastive rather than controlling, and suffix-vowel variants affect closure without changing the target role.

topics.headline: second suffix completes the passive wrath target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the phrase as the necessary target of wrath, with the local referent tied to the wrath-incurred group rather than folded back by default.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence links the second phrase to the passive participle and treats its suffix as the complement of the wrath-incurred group; sound variants do not change that reference.

topics.headline: same upon-form carries adversarial valence here
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same directional surface turning from benefactive to adversarial because the governing expression has changed.
topics.reason: The preposition retains upon-direction, but the wrath context selects adversarial force rather than the benefactive value of the first occurrence.

topics.headline: repeated endpoint audibly binds blessing and wrath
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the same endpoint in both beats and recognizes the moral reversal through repeated grammar.
topics.reason: The two identical preposition-pronoun occurrences create a local echo with opposite semantic charge.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction that carries the second excluded class under the same restrictive frame rather than starting a new narrative unit
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) adds the final negative class as a coordinated counterpart, not as a loose afterthought. Inside the exclusion frame it extends the boundary from wrath-receipt to straying, and its fusion with the following negation makes the movement feel like a nor-unit rather than a neutral and. The path is therefore bounded by cumulative coordination.

topics.headline: conjunction coordinates the second negative class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final class as coordinated under the same exclusion, not appended as a separate gloss.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence coordinates the final active participle with the wrath participle within the excluded group.

topics.headline: coordination and negation arrive as one unit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the conjunction and negation working together as a nor-like expansion of the exclusion.
topics.reason: The local construction pairs the conjunction with the following negator, making coordination and reinforced exclusion arrive together.

words.gloss_range: negative particle that carries the prior exclusion across coordination to the final class and keeps that class outside the requested path
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) keeps the final class inside the same exclusion rather than letting it stand as a permissible alternative path type. Because the exclusion noun is not repeated, this small particle carries the boundary forward with asymmetrical lightness. The compact particle pair then releases into the long final class, so grammar and cadence both make the last exclusion land.

topics.headline: negation extends the exclusion to the final class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second negative class remains under the same restrictive frame as the first.
topics.reason: The negator follows the conjunction and carries the prior exclusion across coordination rather than starting independent clausal negation.

topics.headline: negation blocks false equivalence with the favored route
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final class categorically excluded, not placed beside the favored route as another viable type.
topics.reason: The particle reinforces categorical exclusion of the final group from the requested path.

topics.headline: canonical particle avoids symmetrical repeated exception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second exclusion is structurally lighter and dependent on the first hinge, not a flat repetition of the same exceptive noun.
topics.reason: Variant evidence tests repeated exceptive wording, while the canonical particle keeps the construction asymmetrical.

topics.headline: short negation releases into the long closing word
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the compact negation prepare the acoustic expansion of the final excluded class.
topics.reason: The prosodic row gives a local cadence effect without altering the syntax.

words.gloss_range: definite genitive masculine plural active participle naming the astray as the final excluded class, with straying left absolute rather than tied to an explicit complement
words.root_gloss_range: straying, losing the way, error, forgetting, disappearance, and loss of trace; the local active participle selects ongoing directional drift rather than passive wrath-reception
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلضَّآلِّينَ}} ({{tr:al-ḍāllīna}}) closes the ayah as a genitive coordinated class under the exclusion. Its missing complement makes straying stand as an absolute state, yet the opening path word tells the reader what contrast to recover. The {{ar:ض ل ل}} ({{tr:ḍ-l-l}}) field deepens straying into loss of way, memory, and trace, while the active participle distinguishes this final class from the passive wrath-incurred class. As the last word, it answers the guidance request of 1:6 by naming the anti-direction, gathering the route, favor, and wrath axes into one negative endpoint. Its doubled center and long ending make the final exclusion linger as the route envelope closes.

topics.headline: omitted complement makes straying absolute
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final class is not limited by an explicit from-what phrase; the whole path contrast must be recovered from the ayah.
topics.reason: The local active participle has no explicit complement, so the omission compresses the opening path contrast into the final word.

topics.headline: genitive active participle remains governed by exclusion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final word locked into the coordinated excluded class rather than shifted into a new nominative grammar.
topics.reason: Case and variant evidence confirm the received genitive active participle as the final governed class.

topics.headline: root image expands straying beyond a wrong turn
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels straying as loss of way, memory, and trace, while local grammar keeps the selected sense as the astray class.
topics.reason: Root evidence supplies directional, cognitive, and disappearance imagery, but the local participle names the class rather than activating every branch independently.

topics.headline: final word answers the guidance request
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the surah close the guidance request of 1:6 by naming the direction guidance excludes.
topics.reason: The final word forms the negative pole of the prior guidance request and completes the path-opening to straying-closing frame.

topics.headline: active drift contrasts with passive wrath-reception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader distinguishes two ways of being outside the favored path: wrath borne from without and active drift from within.
topics.reason: The local final word is an active participle and lacks the repeated upon-them endpoint, contrasting with the passive wrath construction before it.

topics.headline: final word gathers path, favor, wrath, and straying axes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final word as the negative endpoint where the ayah's route, favor, and wrath contrasts converge.
topics.reason: The cooccurrence row is locally meaningful because the ayah itself contains those semantic poles in sequence.

topics.headline: geminated and long final cadence seals exclusion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final excluded class linger as the ayah's closing sound.
topics.reason: The sound rows affect cadence and closure while preserving the local grammar and referent.

topics.headline: claim that both negatives are passive constructions
topics.blocking_evidence: The bundle identifies the final word as a genitive masculine plural active participle, not a passive participle.
topics.reason: The row's broader contrast is useful elsewhere, but its claim that the final word is passive conflicts with the local QAC form tag and grammar.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **The path becomes socially embodied.** Lexical evidence: ص ر ط B001, straight road; ن ع م B001, bestowed favor; ع ل م B002 in 1:2, distinguishing mark; ه د ي B001 in 1:6, guidance. Structural cue: 1:6 asks for the path; 1:7 restates it as the path of people, not an abstract route. Assigned role: the favored ones are living markers of the road. Abductive move: the packet supplies road, favor, and sign-marking; I infer that people become waymarks by received favor. Reading change: the path reads as a transmitted social trajectory rather than a private mental direction.

2. **Favor as softening and making the route livable.** Lexical evidence: ن ع م B001, favor/good condition; ن ع م B002, softness/easeful living; ه د ي B004, gracious gift; ق و م B009 in 1:6, subsistence/support. Structural cue: the favored group is opposed to anger and loss. Assigned role: favor makes the path inhabitable, supported, and softened. Abductive move: the packet supplies softness/support and the negative alternatives; I infer that favor alters the material feel of the route. Reading change: أنعمت عليهم reads not only as “gave them blessings” but as “made their way livable and sustained.”

3. **“Not” as active differentiation, not a footnote.** Lexical evidence: غ ي ر B005, otherness/difference/exception/negation; غ ي ر B003, altering/substituting one thing for another. Structural cue: غير stands between the favored path and two failure groups. Assigned role: غير performs the boundary operation that keeps the requested path from being confused with nearby alternatives. Abductive move: the packet supplies difference and substitution; I infer that negation actively changes orientation by excluding false routes. Reading change: the final clause reads as path-engineering through differentiation, not merely as a warning.

4. **Wrath as hardened opposition.** Lexical evidence: غ ض ب B001, intensified anger toward retaliation; غ ض ب B003, defiance/opposition; غ ض ب B004, hard compact rock; ر ح م B001 in 1:1–1:3, tenderness. Structural cue: “angered” is opposed to mercy/favor and placed before “astray.” Assigned role: غضب is a hardened, oppositional state that attracts judgment. Abductive move: the packet supplies anger, defiance, hardness, and earlier tenderness; I infer that wrath marks a hardening against the merciful order. Reading change: المغضوب عليهم reads as people fixed in resistant hardness, not only recipients of an emotion.

5. **Going astray as disappearance, loss, and ownerless wandering.** Lexical evidence: ض ل ل B001, deviation from guidance/aim; ض ل ل B002, hiddenness/disappearance; ض ل ل B003, losing/failing to locate; ض ل ل B005, stray animal in wasteland; ر ب ب B001/B002 in 1:2, owner/caretaker. Structural cue: the surah began with Lord/caretaker and now ends with those who are lost or stray. Assigned role: ضلال is the breakdown of guidance, visibility, ownership, and care. Abductive move: the packet supplies Lord/caretaker and lost/stray branches; I infer that straying is not only error but loss from a care-system. Reading change: الضالين reads as the ownerless/lost condition from which the prayer seeks rescue.

6. **The final contrast as legal-moral settlement.** Lexical evidence: د ي ن B002/B003 in 1:4, recompense and debt; غ ي ر B002, legal compensation alternative; غ ض ب B001, anger toward retaliation; ن ع م B001, benefaction. Structural cue: “Day of dīn” precedes “favored / angered / astray.” Assigned role: the final triad shows the account’s possible settlements: favor, wrath, or loss. Abductive move: the packet supplies recompense/debt/compensation and the triadic outcome; I infer a legal-moral sorting mechanism. Reading change: 1:7 reads as the requested verdict-shape of the worshipper’s account, not only a route description.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Because this is the final ayah, no later ayah supplied a further surprise. Its own backward activation was strong: it reinterpreted earlier mercy as protective kinship, رب as care/ownership, دِين as account-settlement, worship as path-smoothing, and guidance as rescue from disappearance.
reader_a.turkish_prose_synthesis_md: İstenen yol, nimet verilmiş insanların yolu olarak somutlaşır; bu insanlar yolun canlı işaretleri olur. Nimet, sadece ihsan değil, yolu yaşanabilir, yumuşak ve destekli kılan bir lütuftur. “Gayr” kelimesi basit bir “değil”den fazlasını yapar: yolu öteki ihtimallerden ayırır. Gazaba uğrayanlar rahmet düzenine karşı sertleşmiş muhalefeti, dalalette olanlar ise görünürlüğünü, yönünü ve sahibini kaybetmiş başıboşluğu gösterir. Böylece son ayet, bütün surenin talebini açar: rahmetle başlayan söz, bakım ve hesap içinde, kaybolmayan ve sertleşmeyen bir yola çevrilmek ister.

reader_b.activated_readings_md:
1. **The road is identified by marked recipients of favor.** Evidence: `ص ر ط B001` road/path, `ن ع م B001` bestowed favor and pleasant well-being, `ن ع م B003` praise as excellent, and `ع ل م B002` distinguishing mark/landmark from 1:2. Mechanism: the path is not defined abstractly but through “those” upon whom favor has landed; they function as markers that make the road recognizable. The packet supplies path, favor, praise, and sign/landmark branches; I infer that favored people become road-markers. Abductive move: if a path is hard to find, the visible trace of those already favored can identify it. Reading change: “صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم” reads as a marked social route, not merely a class of fortunate people.

2. **Negation splits the path away from retaliation and aimless deviation.** Evidence: `غ ي ر B005` otherness/exception/negation, `غ ض ب B001` intensified anger toward retaliation, and `ض ل ل B001` going astray from guidance/aim. Mechanism: “غير … ولا” creates two exclusions: the path is not the retaliation-field and not the deviation-field. The packet supplies negation, anger, and straying; I infer that the syntax functions as route-separation. Abductive move: guidance must name avoided trajectories as well as desired direction, because error can resemble movement. Reading change: the ayah becomes a boundary-drawing map: favor is read together with explicit separation from anger and loss.

3. **Repair and substitution away from damaged routes.** Evidence: `غ ي ر B003` altering/substituting one thing for another, `غ ي ر B001` repair through provision/watering/setting right, activated by `ر ب ب B002` repair/nurture in 1:2 and `ه د ي B001` guidance in 1:6. Mechanism: غير does more than exclude; it also activates replacement and repair, as if the requested path substitutes a rightly provisioned route for one ending in anger or loss. The packet supplies repair, substitution, nurture, and guidance; I infer a corrective route-change. Abductive move: to be guided is to have one route changed out for another, not only to receive a label saying “wrong.” Reading change: “غير المغضوب” reads as active redirection and repair, not bare negation.

4. **Herding: favored creatures are led; lost creatures become strays.** Evidence: `ن ع م B005` grazing livestock, especially camels; `ض ل ل B005` stray animal in a wasteland; `ه د ي B008` supported/swaying walking and heavy camels; `ر ب ب B014` herd or gathered wild cattle. Mechanism: the animal-material branches convert the social contrast into a pastoral mechanism: favor gathers and leads, while ضلال leaves an animal in a place of loss with no known owner. The packet supplies livestock, straying, supported walking, and herd gathering; I infer the shepherding relation. Abductive move: “upon them” can be read as care resting on a group so that they do not become ownerless strays. Reading change: the final ayah becomes a request to be gathered and led under care, not scattered into wasteland-loss.

5. **Anger as hardened material obstruction.** Evidence: `غ ض ب B004` hard compact rock, `غ ض ب B008` tough hide/folded leather like a shield, activated by `ص ر ط B003` cutting sword passing through and `ق و م B008` straightness. Mechanism: anger is not only affect; its branches materialize as hard compactness that blocks or armors against the path. The packet supplies hard rock/tough hide, cutting-through, and straightness; I infer obstruction. Abductive move: a straight path must cut through or avoid hardened states that retaliation produces. Reading change: “المغضوب عليهم” carries a material image of hardened blockage, not only a moral category.
reader_b.retrospective_surprises_md: Looking back from the end, the basmalah’s mercy now covers even the exclusions: the final negations are not outside mercy but define what merciful guidance saves from. 1:5 also changed the reading of this ayah: the group on the favored path are not passive beneficiaries only; their way is entered through worship, help-seeking, and the smoothing of the path. The most surprising activation was pastoral: `ن ع م B005` and `ض ل ل B005` make favor versus loss feel like gathered herd versus stray animal, which gives “اهدنا” a strongly protective and communal force.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A dependent community turns toward a sovereign divine addressee through worship, service, obedience, and petition.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The devotional relation extends lexically from willing worship into ownership and coercive service, while lordship also carries the countervailing function of nurture.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Petition for Aid and Direction
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Dependents seek assistance and gentle direction toward an upright path, with compassionate benefaction as the answering function.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: requested aid and cooperation `ع و ن:B001/m01`; gentle guidance `ه د ي:B001/m01`; the traversable path `ص ر ط:B001/m01`; uprightness and rectitude `ق و م:B008/m01`; mercy enacted as benefaction `ر ح م:B001/m02`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 1:1 and 1:3 `ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ` / `ٱلرَّحِيمِ` (`ر ح م`); 1:5 `نَسْتَعِينُ` (`ع و ن`); 1:6 `ٱهْدِنَا`, `ٱلصِّرَٰطَ`, and `ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ` (`ه د ي`, `ص ر ط`, `ق و م`); 1:7 `صِرَٰطَ` (`ص ر ط`)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Aid supplies the enabling force, guidance supplies the directing action, the path supplies its object, and straightness supplies the desired state. Mercy turns the request-response structure into beneficent rather than merely administrative rule.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Good is conferred through compassion and maintenance, stabilized as welfare, and answered by praise or recognition.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Tenderness expands into practical provisioning, repair, guardianship, and structural support, while praise can function either as gratitude or as a claim imposed by a patron.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Compassionate Provision and Nurture
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A caregiver feels tenderness, nurtures a dependent over time, guards its affairs, and supplies or repairs what sustains a good condition.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: tenderness and compassion `ر ح م:B001/m01`; beneficent mercy `ر ح م:B001/m02`; conferred blessing `ن ع م:B001/m02`; good condition `ن ع م:B001/m01`; progressive nurture `ر ب ب:B002/m02`; guardianship and care `ق و م:B004/m01`; provision for dependents `غ ي ر:B001/m01`; repair of their equipment `غ ي ر:B001/m03`; practical aid `ع و ن:B001/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Compassion is the motive, progressive nurture and guardianship are the continuing operations, and food, equipment, and assistance are the practical means. Blessing names the resulting condition of the cared-for dependent.
